title: Surface, cut to architecture
summary: A's calm reframe (same head, plate, coda and three struck-symptom strips) drawn in C's high-tech section-cut language: one large isometric drawing in which a warped lattice, the surface where the three symptoms show, resolves into a true grid over a deep block cut into three bays, one under each symptom, and a single red datum seats on the real layer.
addressed: Kept what you loved in A: the head, the FIG. 02 plate with its two-line readout ('Fix the surface, and it returns.' becomes 'Fix the architecture, and it compounds.'), the Surface | Architecture control, and the three strips that strike each symptom and name the layer that really causes it.

Brought in C's high-tech drawing language, limited to one drawing: a 1px isometric section cut with hidden lines drawn dashed, coded callouts, two dimension lines (Surface, a thin span; Architecture, a deep one) and one small title block (Fig. 02 · Section cut · Not to scale).

Restraint instead of clutter: no more than three callouts are on screen at once (the symptoms in Surface, the bays in Architecture). There are no mono paragraphs, spec tables, cell IDs, legend band or frame lines, and over half the plate is open space.

Nothing is too small to read: callout labels are 14px, the mono codes and dimension values 12px, and the smallest text (the strip index) is 11px. The readout and strip titles are 32px. The lede now sits on two lines instead of three, ending without a stray word.

One clear reading path, from left to right and 01 to 03: the three bays sit side by side under their symptoms, the labels run 01 to 03 down one column, and the strips below repeat the same order. The entrance also follows that order (head, then plate, then the drawing, then the tags).

The logo symbol is gone from the figure. A's nested-mark pieces are replaced by the lattice drawing, with no nested corners, steps or core square. The one red element is a single straight datum line along the top of the real layer.

The figure no longer pre-empts the four-layer stack two sections later: the architecture is drawn as three bays side by side, not as stacked layers, so the reframe and the stack each tell their own story.

reference.site: Round 1 · A + C (reframe A 'Surface, then architecture' × reframe C 'Section cut, red plane')
reference.borrowed: From reframe C (Intercom's Fin engine sheet), the way the argument is drawn: a thin surface plane floating over the assembly that really produces it, in 1px true isometric, with coded callouts and two dimension lines contrasting a thin 'surface' with a deep 'architecture'. From reframe A (monday.com's Without | With diagram), the composition: one wide flat plate whose meaning is a two-state toggle, a big two-voice readout at top-left, and the caption band with a segmented control at bottom-right.
reference.kelwin: The drawing is DIRECTION-AC's LATTICE primitive, not the logo. The surface is a 12×6 lattice floating 30 units above the cut. In Surface it is warped (seeded displaced vertices, three bulges where 01 Pipeline, 02 Sales execution and 03 Tooling are pinned, one sag, five missing members) over a true outline and an architecture drawn only in dashed hidden lines. In Architecture every vertex interpolates onto the true grid and the missing members close. The block beneath plots solid and its long face is divided into three bays (01 Narrative architecture, 02 Orchestration, 03 GTM intelligence), each spanning the same four lattice columns as the symptom above it. Dashed drops seat the surface over the cut, two dimensions contrast the thin surface with the deep architecture, and one straight red datum draws along the top of the bays. Callouts are the kit's (Mona 14px with 12px mono code boxes): symptoms on a right-hand column, bays on a left-hand column (label-left form) whose leaders pass beneath the preceding bays, never across them. The title block reads 'Not to scale', which is honest drafting for a conceptual figure. Built on kit-ac: .ac-head, .ac-statement, .ac-plate/.ac-field/.ac-capband, .ac-tblock, .ac-seg, .ac-callout(--l), .ac-dim, .ac-strips, .ac-plot.

motion: entrance (reading order): the margin-to-margin hairline draws and the kit's head choreography runs (label, the two statement lines rising from masks, the red rule, the lede, then the door, 0–700ms). The FIG. 02 plate follows the lede (640ms) in its SURFACE state: the dashed construction (true surface outline, hidden architecture) and the readout 'Fix the surface, and it returns.' fade in. The 20 lattice lines then plot left to right from 860ms (stroke-dashoffset, 760ms each, 24ms stagger), so the warped surface draws itself. The symptom tags fade in 01 → 02 → 03 (from 1.5s, 140ms apart). The strips cascade 01 → 03 beneath (from 1.2s, 80ms stagger).

the one orchestrated moment (at 2.6s, warp resolves to true): the tags lift away (280ms, drifting 10px down: 'look one layer down'). Every one of the 91 lattice vertices then interpolates from its warped position to the true grid (requestAnimationFrame, 1300ms, --ease-inout). This is a real vertex morph, not a crossfade, and the five missing members close as it lands. The cut draws in drafting order: its outline (600ms, 90ms stagger), then the two bay dividers left to right, then the faint face cells. The hidden dashed lines fade out, and the dashed drops and the Surface / Architecture dimensions appear. The bay labels fade in 01 → 03. Last, the red datum draws left to right along the top of the bays (500ms, landing at ≈ 4.5s), while the readout crossfades to 'Fix the architecture, and it compounds.'.
ambient: none. The figure rests once the datum seats.

interaction: Surface | Architecture really switches the figure both ways. Back to Surface, the lattice warps again (900ms), the cut retracts and the tags return. Forward, the full resolve replays. The first click cancels the automatic switch. Kit hovers apply: the link underline turns --fg and its → nudges 3px, and segment labels lift to --fg (a local guard keeps the selected segment legible on hover).

on the live site: the plate opens in Surface. When it is 50% visible (IntersectionObserver, no pin), the lattice plots and the tags pin, and the switch to Architecture fires once ≈ 1.8s later, never again after the first click. Reduced motion renders the resolved Architecture state synchronously, with no timers and no rAF.
notes: The stage is 1400px: 128/128 padding, the kit head (two-line lede), 64px to the plate, a 480px plate (a 424px field that fully contains the drawing, plus the 56px band), and the strips. Lede copy changed slightly so it holds two lines in both skins: 'Most firms treat the surface — campaigns, conversion, reps. Kelwin diagnoses the architecture that produces it.' (treat the symptom, diagnose the cause). DIRECTION-AC's brief asks for 'three labelled levels'; they are drawn as three bays side by side rather than three stacked bands. This keeps the reading path left to right in step with the strips, puts each cause directly under its symptom, and avoids a stacked-layer figure two sections before the stack's STRATA slabs. Geometry is shared by the JS (seeded mulberry32, so renders repeat) and the static final-state markup, which a node script generates from the same functions, so the page is correct with or without JS. Three callouts at a time (≤ 5), two dimension lines (≤ 2), one title block of three cells, and 9 + 2 annotation words. Red: the label square and rule (family punctuation) plus the single datum line. The link is the quiet door, not red. Kit note: .ac-seg > button:hover outranks the selected state, so a hovered selected segment turned white-on-white. This fragment pins it to --bg; the kit should get the same fix (.ac-seg > [aria-selected=true]:hover, [aria-pressed=true]:hover { color: var(--bg) }).
